assumptions: Assay reagents (capture reagents and particle counter) have sufficient sensitivity and are compatible with sample buffers after capture-compatibility validation.
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield exists to run matched bounded fraction and secretome controls and to perform spike-in controls (n >= 3 independent lots recommended).
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and program rodent evidence imply that membrane-protected, particle-associated measurements (capture co-localized with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) distinguish bona fide intact EVs from soluble or non-vesicular co-isolates. Controlling per-sample recovery with an exogenous intact-EV spike-in addresses assay-failure and labeling-artifact competing explanations and enables within-sample discrimination of true absence versus analytical loss.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail orthogonal identity gate (spike-in recovery + endogenous capture co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity)
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity (spike-in-controlled qualitative gate)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: An orthogonal, spike-in–validated co-localized capture + particle + detergent/protease-sensitive signature is the minimal non-numeric identity attribute that enables classifying a preparation as EV-enriched versus secretome-like without asserting potency.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: assay performance, lot variability, and capture-compatibility must be established; does not imply potency.

edges.competing_explanation: Spike-in recovery may validate assay function while endogenous absence could reflect true lot variability rather than fractionation failure.
edges.missing_experiment: Per-lot spike-in-controlled fractionation comparing bounded fraction and secretome control; reproducibility across >=3 lots.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: guidance and rodent data support the rationale but do not prove, for this program, that endogenous activity maps uniquely to a spike-in-validated, membrane-protected signature.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect intact-EV exposure in vivo may reflect administration/labeling limitations rather than absence of intact EVs in the source fraction.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recovery using materials classified as EV-enriched versus secretome by the spike-in identity gate.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: lack of large-animal detectability underscores need to gate identity before expensive bridging; negative biodistribution could reflect route/formulation or labeling factors rather than identity per se.

nodes.statement: If a bounded small-EV fraction contains membrane-protected particles, then an exogenous intact-EV spike-in added before fractionation will be recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and will lose signal after detergent + protease/RNase (assay validation).

If endogenous capture-positive signal co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive in the bounded fraction but not in the secretome-retaining concentrate, then the bounded fraction is analytically distinguishable as EV-enriched and can be treated as a discrete drug-substance identity.

If the bounded fraction fails the spike-in-validated co-localization + detergent/protease-sensitivity pattern, then the preparation is indistinguishable from secretome with respect to intact-EV identity and should not be advanced as an EV-enriched drug-substance.

competing_explanations: Endogenous capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle peaks could reflect co-eluting non-vesicular particles (lipoproteins, aggregates) that bind capture reagents and are detergent-resistant under the chosen conditions.
Negative endogenous signal in bounded fractions despite spike-in recovery could reflect true donor/lot variability rather than fractionation failure.
dependencies: Establish capture-compatibility buffer panels before interpreting capture readouts
Produce >=3 independent pilot conditioned-medium lots with documented source-cell bank/passage
Acquire or prepare a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and validate its orthogonal readout
design_question: Daily question: Can a fraction-level, spike-in–controlled orthogonal identity workflow (exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery + immuno-capture of intact material co-localized with particle-count peaks + detergent/protease protection) produce a reproducible qualitative pass/fail identity gate that classifies a conditioned-medium-derived bounded small-EV fraction as an EV-enriched drug-substance and distinguishes it from a secretome-retaining concentrate?
expected_measurable_effect: A qualitative pass/fail classification per lot: 'pass' when (1) spike-in is recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fraction(s) and is detergent/protease-sensitive and (2) endogenous capture-positive signal co-localizes with particle peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive; 'fail' when these features are absent or endogenous signal is detergent-insensitive despite spike-in recovery.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal fraction-level workflow: (1) add exogenous intact-EV spike-in to samples prior to fractionation; (2) fractionate (iodixanol cushion or SEC) and measure particle counts per fraction; (3) perform immuno-capture on intact fractions and quantify endogenous marker signal and spike-in tracer signal separately; (4) perform protease/RNase protection +/- detergent on captured material for both spike-in tracer and endogenous signal; (5) measure total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched pair from identical conditioned-medium lots: (A) bounded EV-enriched fraction spiked with exogenous intact-EV tracer versus (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) spiked identically. Include detergent+protease-treated aliquots and buffer-only negative controls.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation spiked into buffer and processed in parallel to confirm capture and protection assay performance. Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Capture-compatibility buffer-only controls to detect assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank and passage range
Access to a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in and validated capture reagents with buffer compatibility
Analytical capacity for density-fractionation/SEC, particle counting, immuno-capture, and protection assays
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks across >=3 lots despite validated spike-in recovery (falsification), or inconsistent spike-in recovery preventing assay-controlled discrimination (method failure).
experiment.falsification_outcome: If spike-in recovery is validated but endogenous capture-positive co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive signal are not reproducibly observed in bounded fractions across independent lots, treat the material as indistinguishable from secretome for identity and CMC planning and revise fractionation/source strategies; if spike-in control fails, redesign the spike-in and assay before relying on an identity gate.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An orthogonal intact-EV identity gate consisting of (1) exogenous intact-EV spike-in membrane-protected recovery co-localized with particle-count peaks and (2) endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localization with particle peaks in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the secretome-retaining concentrate will discriminate EV-enriched drug-substance candidates from secretome controls.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization: particle-count peak fraction(s) that are capture-positive and show (A) preserved spike-in tracer signal that is lost after detergent+protease (validating assay recovery and membrane protection) and (B) endogenous capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive in the bounded fraction but not in the secretome control.
experiment.question: Can addition of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in prior to fractionation enable a qualitative, per-lot identity gate that distinguishes a bounded EV-enriched small-EV fraction from a concentrated secretome-retaining conditioned-medium by demonstrating (A) spike-in membrane-protected recovery co-localized with particle peaks and (B) endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localization only in the bounded fraction?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) bounded small-EV enrichment (e.g., TFF->SEC->single-step iodixanol cushion) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium without enrichment (secretome-retaining)
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in (non-overlapping species or isotope-labeled tracer) with QC characterization
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV markers (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents) and buffer-compatibility panels
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane disruption
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered)
Protein:particle ratio differences between bounded fraction and secretome control
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n >= 3 independent conditioned-medium lots)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, (1) the exogenous spike-in tracer is recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and shows loss after detergent+protease (validating assay recovery and membrane protection), and (2) endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior are observed reproducibly in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the secretome-retaining concentrate processed identically. This pattern enables a pass/fail identity gate: bounded fraction = EV-enriched (pass); secretome = not EV-enriched (fail).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Spike-in recovery controls distinguish assay failure or labeling loss from true absence of intact-EV enrichment in bounded fractions.
Inference: A qualitative, orthogonal identity gate enables materially different CMC triage decisions (advance for bridging vs treat as secretome).
falsification_criteria: If the exogenous spike-in is reliably recovered and shows expected detergent/protease sensitivity but endogenous capture-positive signal does not co-localize with particle-count peaks or is detergent-insensitive in the bounded fraction across >=3 independent lots, the hypothesis is falsified and the material must be treated as secretome-like for identity and CMC decisions.
If spike-in recovery is inconsistent across replicates (assay failure), the experimental approach must be redesigned before interpreting identity outcomes.
human_decisions_required: Selection and characterization of the exogenous intact-EV spike-in reagent (species/isotope and tracer readout)
Agree on the qualitative pass/fail rubric and minimum replicate count (recommended n >= 3) for operational identity calls
Decide whether an EV-enriched pass will be sufficient to advance lots into bridging and potency-linkage studies or whether additional criteria are required
manufacturability_assessment: Qualitative: Implementable at fractionation stage using currently available analytical steps (spike-in, fractionation, particle counts, immuno-capture, protection assays). Yield and throughput implications must be assessed in pilot GMP-like runs before adoption as an operational gate.
manufacturing_rationale: A qualitative, spike-in–validated identity gate enables a binary manufacturing decision (advance lot for bridging / potency linkage versus reject or reprocess) without prematurely defining numeric release limits. This gate is implementable at the fractionation stage (bounded small-EV fraction vs concentrated secretome) and informs whether to treat material as an EV drug-substance for subsequent stability, potency, and scale comparability work.
measurement_strategy: Per-lot, run matched paired processing from the same conditioned-medium lot: (A) bounded small-EV fraction and (B) concentrated conditioned-medium (secretome-retaining), each spiked identically with an exogenous, characterized intact-EV tracer prior to fractionation. Measure particle counts per fraction, immuno-capture signal for endogenous markers and spike-in tracer on intact fractions, and assess detergent + protease/RNase sensitivity for both spike-in and endogenous signals. Report a qualitative pass/fail identity call per lot based on the composite criteria. Include buffer-compatibility controls and spike-in recovery thresholds (qualitative: recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered).
novelty_statement: Novelty: This hypothesis requires an explicit per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in combined with fraction-level co-localized capture + particle-count + detergent/protease protection to produce a binary, operational identity gate. Prior program hypotheses proposed orthogonal intact-EV analytics or spike-ins separately; this proposal uniquely couples a spike-in recovery control with fraction-level co-localization and protection readouts as the minimal, testable qualitative gate to decide whether a given conditioned-medium-derived bounded fraction should be treated as an EV-enriched drug-substance candidate for downstream CMC and bridging decisions. This is not a cosmetic rewording of prior experiments because it mandates within-sample spike-in validation as a discriminating control and sets a clear, binary pass/fail identity outcome tied to per-lot advancement.
principal_risks: Assay incompatibility between capture reagents and formulation buffers could create false negatives; buffer-compatibility controls are required.
Spike-in tracer design must avoid cross-reactivity and must be robustly characterized; poor spike-in performance undermines the gate.
A qualitative identity gate may still fail to predict in vivo intranasal recoverability across species; bridging experiments remain necessary.
proposed_potency_relationship: None asserted. This proposal defines a product-identity gate only; any potency linkage must be tested in follow-on experiments and is not assumed here.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt an orthogonal, non-numeric product-identity gate defined by: (A) recovery of an exogenous, characterized intact-EV spike-in that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is lost after detergent + protease/RNase (validating assay recovery and membrane protection), and (B) endogenous immuno-capture-positive signal for canonical EV surface markers on intact material that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is substantially reduced or abolished after detergent + protease/RNase in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in concentrated secretome-retaining concentrates. Use this composite pass/fail gate to classify preparations as 'EV-enriched (pass)' versus 'secretome-like (fail)' for downstream CMC comparability and gating decisions (non-numeric).
title: Spike-in validated, fraction-level intact-EV identity gate that discriminates an EV-enriched bounded small-EV drug-substance from secretome-retaining conditioned medium
